summary: Feed s112_double is degraded: VLAN 20 is completely absent (50% packets untagged) and 93.9% encrypted traffic exceeds NDR 90% tolerance. Bidirectional flow, deduplication, drops and tool load are healthy, but VLAN gap and encryption blindness limit NDR detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN/TAP is stripping 802.1Q tags or VLAN 20 is not forwarded to this NDR tool port. 50% untagged packets with 0 packets of VLAN 20 seen indicates trunk not preserved or broker VLAN filter/policy dropping VLAN 20, not a sampling artifact.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR has zero visibility into required VLAN 20, losing ~50% of expected traffic. Detections for lateral movement, east-west and segment-specific threats on VLAN 20 will not fire.

recommended_fix.why: NDR requires both VLAN 10 and 20 with tags preserved. Configure broker ingress to preserve 802.1Q and explicitly forward VLAN 20 trunk to this tool port; disable tag stripping.

findings.root_cause: 94% of bytes are encrypted (TLS), above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is predominantly TLS 1.2/1.3 without broker-side decryption or key sharing, so payload is opaque to the NDR.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR is limited to metadata/flow analysis and cannot inspect payloads for malware, C2, or exfiltration. Detection efficacy drops sharply as most sessions are opaque.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt at the packet broker (or forward session keys) and send cleartext copy to NDR, or deploy NDR with integrated TLS visibility. Selective decryption for VLANs 10/20 preserves privacy while restoring payload inspection.
